samples.summary: Find-bar replace path has no read-only gate and bypasses the EditorAPI read-only neutralization entirely
samples.evidence: `DocsFindBar` takes no `readOnly` prop and `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (docs-find-bar.tsx:121,130 — both touched by this diff) call `state.replaceActive()` / `state.replaceAll()` on a `FindReplaceState` built from `editor.getDoc()` and `editor.getStore().snapshot()` (lines 54-57). That writes the CRDT directly, skipping every guard the codebase relies on for viewers: the `MUTATING_METHODS` no-op allowlist at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4018-4036` and all `TextEditor` `readOnly` guards. The diff wires `editor?.clearImageSelection()` into exactly these two handlers and the accompanying design text (`docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md`) blesses the seam as "runs straight against the `Doc` the find bar holds ... bypassing the editor's own mutation entry points" — but no permission check was added alongside it. Attacker path: a `viewer`-role share link (`shared-document.tsx:278` `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`) renders `DocsView` read-only; the find bar is opened with Cmd/Ctrl+F (deliberately allowed in read-only, `text-editor.ts:903`) and, if `showReplace` is ever true, the Replace / All buttons write to the shared document. Today the only thing preventing that is that `showReplace` is set solely by `onFindReplaceRequest`, whose Cmd/Ctrl+H keydown falls after the `readOnly` early-return at `text-editor.ts:894-912`, so I could not complete the exploit through the shipped UI — the boundary is one unrelated keydown branch in another package, with no gate at the mutation itself. This matters more than usual here because the branch's own docs state the server-side Yorkie auth webhook defaults to shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset ⇒ allow, `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:87`), making the client `readOnly` flag the effective write boundary for anonymous share links. Suggested fix: pass `readOnly` into `DocsFindBar` and early-return in both handlers (and hide the replace row), mirroring `showCut`/`showPaste` gating in `docs-context-menu.tsx`.

samples.summary: Read-only enforcement is an API-surface allowlist while `getDoc()`/`getStore()` hand out unguarded mutation handles
samples.evidence: `initialize()` neutralizes read-only by overwriting a hardcoded `MUTATING_METHODS` list with no-ops (editor.ts:4018-4036), but the same `api` exposes `getDoc(): Doc` (editor.ts:53) and `getStore(): DocStore` (editor.ts:55) with no gating, so any consumer can call `doc.insertText/deleteText/applyInlineStyle` or `store.snapshot()/update()` on a read-only mount. That is the mechanism the find-bar replace path (finding above) uses, and it means the allowlist reads as an enforced boundary while actually being a convenience wrapper. Pre-existing rather than introduced here, but the diff both leans on it (`docs-find-bar.tsx` mutating via `editor.getDoc()`) and adds a new API entry (`clearImageSelection`) without revisiting the list. Worth either gating the raw handles in read-only (e.g. returning a frozen/read-only Doc view) or documenting them as an explicit trusted escape hatch with a lint/arch rule on their callers.
searchedFor: grep getDoc()|getStore() call sites across packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: Read-only pending-link href can survive a press and be consumed by an unrelated later mouseup, opening a document-controlled URL
samples.evidence: The new `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` call in the image branch of `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2665) stores `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` on mousedown; `TextEditor.handleMouseUp` consumes it and calls `window.open(href, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` (text-editor.ts:2005-2015). `handleMouseUp` is bound to `container` (text-editor.ts:579), so if the press starts on a hyperlinked image and the button is released outside the container, no mouseup consumes or clears the stored href. A later press that returns before either recorder — e.g. a right-click, which exits at `e.button !== 0` in `handleImageMouseDown` and at `e.button === 2` in `handleMouseDown` (text-editor.ts:1668) — still produces a mouseup that opens the stale, document-authored URL in a new tab, i.e. navigation the viewer did not ask for on that click. Scheme abuse is bounded by `isSafeUrl`, so this is unintended-navigation/phishing-surface rather than script execution. The stale-href hazard pre-dates this change for text links; the diff widens the set of presses that arm it (images, in read-only) and routes them through a path where `handleMouseDown` — which would otherwise reset the field — never runs. Clearing `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` on a mouseup that did not follow a matching mousedown (or binding the consumer to `document`) closes it.

verdict.reason: The replace handlers are unreachable for a read-only viewer, because a read-only gate does exist on the only path that enables them. handleReplace/handleReplaceAll have callers exclusively inside the `{showReplace && ...}` block (docs-find-bar.tsx:277, 286, 291, 298). Repo-wide, `findBarShowReplace` is set true in exactly one place — the `editor.onFindReplaceRequest` callback at docs-view.tsx:430-432 — and `onFindReplaceRequest` is fired from exactly one place, text-editor.ts:1075 (`case 'h'`), which sits after the read-only early return at text-editor.ts:894-912 (non-navigation keys return at :909, permitting only Cmd/Ctrl+A and Cmd/Ctrl+F). The editor's `readOnly` is stable and correctly sourced for viewers: shared-document.tsx:278 derives it from an already-resolved link, passes it to DocsView (:308), which forwards it to initialize() (docs-view.tsx:327) and into TextEditor (editor.ts:2276), so there is no window where the flag is false for a viewer. Additionally the authoritative server-side write gate exists and denies rw for non-editor share roles (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:164-200), consistent with the explicit design note at editor.ts:4016-4017 that client-side readOnly is a convenience, not the boundary. Hardening DocsFindBar with a readOnly prop is defensible, but there is no reachable viewer path to the CRDT mutation, so this is not a blocking authorization bypass under the security rubric.

finding.summary: Server-side write authorization for viewer share links is shadow-mode by default, so the client `readOnly` flag this change widens is the only effective write boundary
finding.evidence: `YorkieAuthController` computes the per-document read/write decision but returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (constructor at :86-88, shadow branch at :97-105); packages/backend/README.md:111 documents `false` as the default. `readOnly` in the frontend is derived purely client-side (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:152`, `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'`) and passed into `initialize()`. In a default deployment, therefore, any client-side read-only gap in the docs editor is a real write for an anonymous viewer, not a UX inconsistency. This is pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the assumption the change under review leans on: the diff deliberately opens `handleImageMouseDown`, the textarea focus and the key/clipboard handlers to viewers and compensates entirely with client-side `readOnly` checks (the design doc it adds says so explicitly at docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:292). Reported so the widened surface is weighed against the enforcement posture rather than assumed to be backstopped by the server.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the repository. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88 defaults `enforce` to false unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', and :97-105 converts every computed deny into `{allowed: true, reason: 'shadow'}`. The discarded decision is the only server-side viewer/editor write distinction for anonymous share visitors (:200, `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`). backend/README.md:111 documents false as the default, and no .env.example or deployment manifest in the repo sets it to true, so a default deployment does not enforce. Frontend readOnly is derived purely client-side (shared-document.tsx:152 and :278) and the change's own design doc concedes the client flag is the effective write boundary in shadow mode (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:299-302). The chain is completable without any UI: auth.controller.ts:76-83 mints a Yorkie share token for any share-link token regardless of role, and auth.service.ts:75-77 carries no role, so a viewer-link holder can attach with verb 'rw' via the Yorkie SDK and the webhook allows it. This is a missing/weakened permission gate on the enforced path — squarely in the authorization lane — and I found no guard elsewhere making it unreachable. Pre-existing and out-of-diff status is not a refutation ground under the stated instructions.
